description.narrative:
Project description April 2025 – December 2025 This collaboration is a continuation of our work around postgrowth with politicians and trade unions across Europe. In follow up to the earlier collaboration in 2023 and 2024, where we built the network byorganising a series of roundtables, public events, and developing primers on postgrowth <(>&<)> policy, this project expands and shifts the focus of our joint activities. The main objectives of the network have been: ● Provide a space to exchange for politicians across Europe that are working on postgrowth policies at national level ● Build a policy agenda for postgrowth, and to develop shared insights on skills and strategies for implementing postgrowth policies at the national level ● Connect Trade Unions the postgrowth policy discussion. In a next phase we will continue to pursue these objectives but also intend to focus more on strategy development and coalition building. We foresee all the activities to develop in close collaboration between CommonsNetwork and Oxfam.
* Evaluation and strategy development Current times demand reflection and strategy work. We need to evaluate our strategy and to decide where to focus our energy and resources in the next period. The changing political context requires us to adapt and sharpen our political narrative, to rethink our target audience and alliances, and to set up a coherent short- and medium-term agenda for postgrowth policies. CN and Oxfam Novib have started this process with IPE and PolicyLab, two potential new partners in the project, and would like to include members of the network in this process as well. Our main avenue for spearheading this effort is through strategy and coalition workshops. We will start out with a smaller one with key partnersand this will be followed by a larger one. These will be live and mostlikely both take place in the Netherlands. Partners we have in mins for the 2nd workshop are Oxfam European working group for new economy, WEALL, Political foundations, XR en Housing movements, Trade Unions: ETUC en ETUI -

participating-org.narrative: Mission <(>&<)> VisionCommons Network is a collaboratory for the social and ecological transition. They explore new models for economy and society in order to collectively transform the system and shape a caring and just future. They bring together people and ideas and provide tools and insights for social movements, governments and civil society. A just and caring economy Commons Network aims to enhance the democratisation and social ecological transition of the economy. Instead of continuing to struggle to "green" growing economies, we need to get out of growth thinking and fundamentally redesign the economy. The digital dimension is a crucial part of this, as technology has come to shape our economy. Such a transition requires policies but also embracing other practices. Practices that redefine work and value creation. This means recognizing and valuing care work in the household and beyond. But also investing in the local economy and the cooperative sector where citizens unite around providing basic needs such as energy, food and shelter in a self-organizing way. This domain is also called the commons: it is a forgotten and underexposed sector in the economy alongside that of the market and the state.
